data_description.enable_gateway_monitoring: Each poll, ping the gateway and the next two hops toward the internet: latency, jitter and packet loss.
data_description.enable_dns_monitoring: Each poll, time one uncached lookup at the DNS server below.
data_description.dns_server: Server whose lookup time is measured. Auto-detect uses the one this host is configured with.
data_description.ping_count: Pings sent to each target every poll (1 to 10). More pings give steadier readings and finer packet loss.
data_description.hop_ownership: Off by default. Shows the network operator (ASN) of each public hop. Sends those hop addresses (your ISP's routers, not your own address) to Team Cymru's free IP-to-ASN service, through your DNS server. Private and shared ISP addresses have no owner and are never sent.
data_description.usage_totals: Off by default. Adds six diagnostic sensors: pings sent, traceroutes run, DNS queries sent, speed tests run, and speed test data downloaded and uploaded, counted since install. Counting goes on while this is off.
data_description.long_term_statistics: Off by default. Keeps hourly statistics of latency, jitter, packet loss, DNS latency and speed test readings, for trends over months; Home Assistant never deletes them. Off, history still covers the last 10 days. Turning it off later makes Home Assistant warn once per sensor until you delete its statistics in Developer tools > Statistics.
data_description.speed_test_backend: Off by default. A test downloads and uploads for up to 10 s each way with the chosen service, which sees your public IP address. M-Lab publishes every result with that address, permanently; you are asked to confirm. Cloudflare says it truncates that address to /24 (IPv4) or /48 (IPv6), and IHM sends it no results. LibreSpeed uses volunteer servers. IHM is not affiliated with any of them. The next screen sets when tests run and how much data they may use.

speed_test.title: Speed tests
speed_test.description: Run speed test and automations start a test at any time. Last test: {last_test}. Each test may use up to {limit_mb} MB, so automatic tests run every {every_days} day(s), using at most {monthly_gb} GB in any 30 days. Before the first test, the automatic limit is 500 MB. The rules: README, How much data speed tests use.

data_description.speed_test_automatic: At a random time between 1 and 5 am, when the line is likely quiet: weekly with no data budget; with one, as often as the budget holds every test. Off: tests run only from Run speed test or an automation.
data_description.speed_test_data_limit_mb: 0 for automatic: each direction gets what 10 s at the last test's speed used, plus 25%, within the budget. Or 100 to 10000 MB, both directions together; each direction stops at half. A test the limit ends is shorter and less precise.
data_description.speed_test_daily_limit: A cap, not a schedule: once this many tests ran in the last 24 hours, more are refused until the oldest is a day old (1 to 40). Counts automatic tests, the button and automations. M-Lab asks automated tests to stay at 4 or fewer.
data_description.speed_test_budget_gb: 0 for none. Sets how often automatic tests run, and a test starts only if it fits in what is left of this after the last 30 days of speed tests. If your plan has a data cap, keep this to a small share of it.

mlab_consent.title: M-Lab publishes your results
mlab_consent.description: M-Lab publishes every test result, including your public IP address and the date and time, and keeps it indefinitely (measurementlab.net/privacy). Confirm to use M-Lab, or close this dialog and choose another service.

data.mlab_consent: I agree to M-Lab publishing my results

traceroute_missing.title: traceroute is not installed
traceroute_missing.description: Internet Health Monitor needs `traceroute` to find hops 2 and 3, so those sensors stay unknown. Install it on the Home Assistant host (`apt install traceroute` or `apk add traceroute`), then reload the integration. Gateway and DNS monitoring keep working.
